cell.definition: The basic membrane-bound structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms, containing cytoplasm, DNA, organelles, and mitochondria.
cell.example: Eukaryotic cells contain a nucleus enclosed within a membrane and produce ATP energy.

cell.definition: A device capable of generating electrical current and voltage from chemical reactions using electrodes, anode, cathode, and electrolyte.
cell.example: A voltaic battery consists of multiple electrochemical cells connected in series.

cell.definition: A small room in which a prisoner is locked up inside a prison or jail facility.
cell.example: The guard locked the inmate inside the concrete prison cell.

network.definition: A computational model of interconnected artificial neurons or nodes with weighted connections trained via backpropagation and gradient descent.
network.example: Deep neural networks learn hierarchical representations from training data.

network.definition: A system of interconnected computers, routers, and hosts exchanging digital data packets using communication protocols like TCP/IP and HTTP.
network.example: ARPANET was the first wide-area packet-switching computer network.

network.definition: A group of people who exchange professional information and contacts, or a chain of television broadcasting stations.
network.example: She built a strong professional network of colleagues across the industry.

weight.definition: A numerical coefficient or parameter in a mathematical model, graph edge, or neural network that scales the importance of an input feature.
weight.example: Backpropagation adjusts the synaptic weights of the neural network to minimize error.

weight.definition: The downward force exerted on the mass of a physical object by gravity, measured in newtons or kilograms.
weight.example: An astronaut experiences weightlessness in orbital microgravity.

protocol.definition: A formal set of digital rules and packet formats governing data transmission between devices over a network, such as TCP/IP, HTTP, or DNS.
protocol.example: The TCP/IP protocol suite guarantees reliable packet delivery over the Internet.

protocol.definition: The official procedure or system of rules governing affairs of state, diplomatic ceremonies, or an amendment to an international treaty.
protocol.example: Ambassadors must follow strict diplomatic protocol during state visits.

nucleus.definition: A membrane-enclosed organelle found in eukaryotic cells that houses the organism's genetic DNA chromosomes and regulates gene expression.
nucleus.example: Unlike prokaryotes, eukaryotic cells store their DNA inside a defined nucleus.

nucleus.definition: The positively charged dense core of an atom composed of protons and neutrons bound by the strong nuclear force.
nucleus.example: Nuclear fission splits the heavy atomic nucleus of uranium into smaller nuclei.

packet.definition: A formatted unit of digital data routed across a packet-switched computer network containing a header (source/destination IP) and payload.
packet.example: Routers forward each packet independently across the network toward its destination IP address.

packet.definition: A small paper or foil pouch containing a measured portion of food, seeds, or powder.
packet.example: He opened a packet of sugar for his coffee.

power.definition: Repeated multiplication or matrix iteration (such as the power method for eigenvectors and PageRank) or statistical explanatory capability.
power.example: The power iteration method converges to the dominant eigenvector of a stochastic matrix.

power.definition: Metabolic energy capacity supplied to living cells by mitochondria and ATP molecules.
power.example: Mitochondria act as the power plants of the eukaryotic cell by synthesizing ATP.
